text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- Free Democrat president Gabor Kuncze intends to have Prime Minister Gyula Horn convene a meeting of the coalition consultation council, to discuss the administration of social insurance, the agreement with the Vatican and the main figures of the 1998 budget.
- At its weekly meeting today the cabinet is expected to discuss next year's budget guidelines in a first reading.
- Opposition MPs continued to argue in favor of delaying the introduction of pension reform while coalition MPs rejected the charges, referring to the need to introduce it early next year.
- The Young Democrats will issue an opposition declaration tonight, in an attempt to formulate the basis of a common strategy for creating a civil Hungary.
- Parliament's constitutional committee gave the green light Wednesday to Janos Nemeth and Istvan Bagi to be appointed to the Constitutional Court.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny said that the Constitutional Court ruling striking down some aspects of the social insurance law will cost the sector five to seven billion forints.
- Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy yesterday fired deputy state secretary Lajos Buzassy, over the question of a diploma obtained by him "under dubious circumstances."
- The Foreign Ministry fired former ambassador to Chile Adolf Szeles Wednesday and initiated court proceedings on a charge of large-scale embezzlement.
- Consumer prices went up by 1.3 percent last month, the year-on-year increase was 17.7 percent.
- The cabinet will consider Finance Ministry 1998 budget draft figures that indicate a reduced state income and higher expenditures for the year.
- National oil and gas company MOL has discovered a new medium-heavy crude oil field near Savoly, southwest Hungary.
- TDK opened the company's new transformer and ferrite factory in Retsag, some 100 kilometers north of Budapest.
- The Austrian savings bank Osterreichische Postsparkasse (OP) will not participate in the impending capital increase in Postabank Rt.
- The Christian Democrat Mayor of Fuzesabony, eastern Hungary, has resigned after making an erotic videocassette starring himself.
